perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- Ethan is a plumber; Gary Guo is his close friend since middle school, and Gary is a doctor.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned and invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation.
- Ethan told Gary that his health matters, that they had been friends a long time, that he hated seeing Gary like this, and that the retreat might give him a new perspective.
- Ethan heard Gary initially decline, saying he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more going on than professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge.
- Gary told Ethan it was complicated and that he did not want to burden him.
- Gary later opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges.
- Ethan felt relief and empathy, suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities, and offered to help Gary organize his schedule.
- Gary agreed, saying he could use help making time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, and saw Gary making efforts to change. Ethan felt hopeful and proud.
- Ethan told Gary he was proud of his progress and that he was there whenever Gary needed to talk. Gary told him things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had had time for a movie.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy.
- Ethan decided to step back but told Gary he was always just a call away and knew Gary had this. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without his support, and felt more in control.
